entry.name: poly~
entry.description: Use the poly~ to encapsulate a patcher inside an object box, to specify the patcher filename and the number of instances you want to load as arguments to the poly~ object, and to control object processing and routing in the loaded patcher instances.

arguments.name: patcher-name
arguments.digest: Name of a patcher to be loaded
arguments.description: The first argument must specify the name of a patcher to be loaded which already exists and is in the Max search path. A subpatch window is not automatically opened for editing when a patcher argument is supplied for theobject.

arguments.name: number-of-instances
arguments.digest: Number of patcher instances to be loaded
arguments.description: The number of patcher instances corresponds to the number of available "voices" This number can be any number between 1 and 1023, and may be dynamically changed by using themessage.

arguments.name: 'up' and up-sampling-factor
arguments.description: Use theargument followed by a number which is a power of two to upsample local DSP processing on the currently loaded patcher (e.g.,specifies 88200 Hz at a sampling rate of 44100 Hz). Upsampling may be dynamically changed by using themessage.

arguments.name: 'down' and down-sampling factor
arguments.description: Use theargument followed by a number which is a power of two to downsample local DSP processing on the currently loaded patcher (e.g.,specifies 22050 Hz at a sampling rate of 44100 Hz). Downsampling may be dynamically changed by using themessage.

arguments.name: 'args' and list-of-argument-values
arguments.description: Use the argumentfollowed by an argument value to initialize any pound-sign arguments in the loaded patcher (e.g.,). If used, theargument must be the last argument word used; everything which appears after the wordwill be treated as an argument value.

attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: args
attributes.digest: Arguments for the Loaded Patch
attributes.description: When using messages to specify arguments for aobject's loaded patch, the patch must be reloaded by setting theattribute for new arguments to take effect after initial load.

attributes.description: When enabled, Parameters defined via classical Parameter objects, likeorwithturned on, will not appear in the top-level patcher's Parameter list. Parameters defined via theobject will always be published to the top-level.Filtered parameters will appear in a-local Parameter list, similar to how Parameters appear inside of theobject.

choices.label: Only Parameters defined byobjects will appear in the top-level patcher's Parameter Window.

attributes.name: legacynotemode
attributes.digest: Legacy Note Mode
attributes.description: When set to 1,allows note and midinote messages to use the old (pre Max 8) voice assignment algorithm, which continues to play voice 1. When set to 0, note and midinote messages cycle through the least recently used voice.

attributes.name: midimode
attributes.digest: Send MIDI Events to All Voices
attributes.description: When midimode is set to '1', all MIDI messages sent towill be sent to all voices. Note that this does not apply tomessages. In order to send allmessages to all voices, use a '-1' value for the voice argument, eg: 'mpeevent 1 1 2 210 117' (an aftertouch message to all voices).

attributes.name: mpemode
attributes.digest: Use MPE Channel as Voice
attributes.description: When this attribute is set to '1',will perform direct voice allocation based on the voice argument of an mpeevent message.

attributes.name: parallel
attributes.digest: Parallel Processing Toggle
attributes.description: When this attribute is set to enable parallel processing, theobject enables the use of multiple threads to run audio processing for all patcher instances. If disabledruns all patcher instances in the audio processing thread. The DSP chain must be restarted whenever the parallel attribute is changed. This attribute is disabled it when Max is hosted by the Live application.At this time, you cannot specify a single subpatcher on a different core. When enabled, this attribute splits up the number of voices between the number of processors available. It is primarily intended for patches that use a significant amount of CPU within multiple voices of the sameobject, and the multithreading overhead is primarily useful for larger signal vector sizes (at least 32 or greater). Other situations will not benefit. Using the default threadcount (which is equal to the number of physical cores) is best.

attributes.name: patchername
attributes.digest: Patcher File(s)
attributes.description: Sets the filename(s) of a patcher file or files loaded into theobject. Theobject can load different patchers on different voices, specified as arguments to the patchername/patchernames attribute. If there is no voices argument to, the total number of patchers specified by the typed-inattribute will be the number of voices; if there is a voices argument, then patchers are repeated in a cycle up to the voice number. You cannot increase the number of voices inby supplying more filenames to theattribute than there are voices. However, you can use theattribute to increase the number of voices before setting the value of.

attributes.description: Toggles the use of high-quality resampling filters. These filters are enabled by default.

attributes.name: size
attributes.digest: Common Max box / inspector attribute (shared across objects; not necessarily listed in this object’s refpage XML).

attributes.name: steal
attributes.digest: Voice Stealing Enable
attributes.description: Voice stealing enable causes theobject sends the data from theormessages to instances that are still marked "busy"; this can result in clicks depending on how the instances handle the interruption. Voice stealing is disabled by default.

attributes.name: target
attributes.digest: Target Voice Number
attributes.description: Theinstance that will receive subsequent messages (other than messages specifically used by theobject itself) arriving at theobject's inlets - for example, The messageroutes messages to the second instance. If themessage specifies a value greater than the current number of instances (copies) of the loaded patcher, the message will be sent to the highest numbered instance (e.g., sending the messageto aobject containing only a single instance will send subsequent messages to the first instance). The messagesends input toinstances, and using any negative number value with themessage will disable input to all instances.

attributes.name: voices
attributes.digest: Number of Voices

attributes.name: vs
attributes.digest: Signal Vector Size for the Loaded Patch
attributes.description: Specifies the signal vector size for theobject's loaded patch. The signal vector size will be set on the next compilation of the DSP chain. Themessage does not force a recompilation of the DSP chain.specifies no fixed vector size. The default is the current signal vector size.

attributes.name: zone
attributes.digest: MPE Zone Select
attributes.description: Use this attribute to set the MPE 'zone' that thewill listen to. The default is '0' (ignore zones).

messages.name: (drag)
messages.digest: Load a file when dragging a patch from the Max File Browser
messages.description: Loads a file when dragging a patch from the Max File Browser to aobject.

messages.name: (mouse)
messages.digest: Open a display window to view loaded patch contents
messages.description: Double-clicking on theopens a display window where you can view the contents of a loaded patcher.

messages.name: allnotesoff
messages.digest: Disable all currently playing notes
messages.description: Disables all playing notes by sending a message to each instance with a playing note consisting of the MIDI pitch most recently received via theormessage followed by a zero velocity (note off message).

messages.name: anything
messages.digest: TEXT HERE
messages.description: The number of inlets and outlets foris determined by the patcher that is loaded. The inlets for the patcher loaded by aobject accept both signal and event connections.The signals are routed inside of the loaded patcher by using theobjects for signals or theobject for events. The total number of inlets in aobject is determined by the highest number of anorobject in the loaded patcher (e.g., if there is anwith argument 3 and anwith argument 4, theobject will have four inlets. All the inlets accept signal connections even though there may not be anobject corresponding to each inlet.Signal inputs are fed to all instances.

messages.name: assignpatcher
messages.digest: Load patcher into a specific voice
messages.description: Useto load a named patcher into a numbered voice location, leaving patchers assigned to other voices unchanged. Themessage cannot be used increase the number of voices -- its first voice number argument must be between 1 and the current total voice count. Moreover,will only work once a patcher has been loaded into the first instance of theeither via an argument or theattribute.After themessage has been used the contents of theattribute will be modified to contain named patchers for each current voice.

messages.name: bang
messages.digest: Send a bang to the patcher loaded into theobject.
messages.description: Sends a bang to the patcher loaded into theobject. The result of the message is determined by the loaded patcher.

messages.name: busymap
messages.digest: Report voice busy states
messages.description: Reports the voice busy state for the number specified as the argument out the specified message outlet of theobject.

messages.name: bypass
messages.digest: Bypassprocessing.
messages.description: Pass through incoming signals. The first argument specifies the voice, and the second argument specifies the state. To bypass all voices, send the message 'bypass 0 1'.

messages.name: down
messages.digest: Downsample the audio on the currently loaded patcher
messages.description: Use themessage followed by a number which is a power of two to downsample local DSP processing on the currently loaded patcher (e.g.,specifies 22050 Hz at a sampling rate of 44100 Hz). Downsampling is not dynamic. DSP must be restarted before the change can take effect. Although bothandare permissible messages to theobject, themessage takes precedence over.

messages.name: exclude
messages.digest: Exclude a voice from note allocation
messages.description: Sending the word, followed by a voice number and a one, prevents ainstance from being sent messages via note allocation when thereceives aormessage. By default, all voices are enabled for note allocation. The word, followed by a voice number and a zero re-enables the instance to receive messages when thereceives aormessage.

messages.name: float
messages.digest: Perform patcher-specific functions
messages.description: Performs functions which are specific to the user-designedpatcher itself.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Perform patcher-specific functions
messages.description: Performs functions which are specific to the user-designedpatcher itself.

messages.name: list
messages.digest: Send a list to a poly instance
messages.description: To send a message to ainstance that starts with one of the words used to control theobject itself, begin the message with the word. For example, the messagesent to the left inlet ofwill outputout the outlet of allobjects, rather than changing the current target instance to the second patcher.

messages.name: midievent
messages.digest: Send a MIDI event to avoice
messages.description: The word, followed by two to four numbers, sends a MIDI event to. The first three number arguments are the bytes of the MIDI message. The fourth, optional, argument is a detune parameter used for MIDI note messages.messages are intended to be used with theobject.

messages.name: midinote
messages.digest: Send a MIDI note event or list of values to ainstance
messages.description: Themessage is followed by two or more values. While note values are ordinarily two numbers that specify a MIDI note number and a velocity value, any numbers may be used for patches which work differently than the standard MIDI model.If the second note value is not 0, theobject routes the pitch velocity to the first available instance. If the velocity is 0 (i.e. a MIDI note-off message), the pitch velocity will be sent to theinstance that generated the note. To determine which instance of the loaded patcher themessage will be sent to, send a(non-busy) or(busy) message to aobject located in the loaded patcher.

messages.name: mpeevent
messages.digest: MPE Event Message
messages.description: The MPE event message is a list composed of the symbol, followed by 6 integers which specify the Zone First Channel, Zone Index, Voice Number, Channel Number, MIDI Message Number, and Data. This message can be sent to a patch encapsulated in aobject using theobject.

messages.name: mute
messages.digest: Mute processing for a patcher instance
messages.description: Turns off signal processing for the specified instance of of a patcher loaded by theobject and sends amessage to theobject for the specified instance. Sending aas the second argument turns the patcher instance on. The messagemutes all instances, andturns on signal processing for all instances of the patcher. If all are muted using amessage, individual instances cannot be unmuted until all are unmuted with amessage.

messages.name: mutemap
messages.digest: Report voice mutes out of a specifiedmessage outlet

messages.name: note
messages.digest: Send data to an available voice instance
messages.description: The word, followed by a message, will send the data to the firstobject of the first instance of the patcher that has not marked itself "busy" by sending ato aobject inside the patcher instance.

messages.name: notemessage
messages.digest: Send an individual note control message
messages.description: Themessage is used to send messages to each active voice (i.e. an individual instances of a subpatcher loaded by theobject). The message is sent directly to theobject by means ofobjects (When addressing aobject, the firstobject in the subpatcher is reserved formessages). Sequentially,messages follow amessage - the first argument of that message being taken as a pitch for the ID of subsequentmessages. Themessages can be of arbitrary length, and may be unpacked and routed inside the subpatcher. In situations where a note-off message that involves a time duration before its completion (e.g. by the use of anobject),messages will be received for processing until the voice is turned off.Note: The only way to turn a voice off properly when using ais to use a signal to aobject in the subpatcher loaded by theobject (if a signal isconnected to theobject , the MIDI note-off message turns off the voice assignment immediately).

messages.name: open
messages.digest: Open a patcher instance for viewing
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, opens the specified instance of the patcher. You can view the activity of any instance of the patcher up to the number of voices (set by themessage or by an argument to theobject). With no arguments, themessage opens the instance that is currently the target (see themessage).

messages.name: setvalue
messages.digest: Direct a message to an individual voice
messages.description: The word, followed by both an instance index (starting at 1) and any message, sends the message to an individual voice of within the MC wrapper., followed by a message, sends the message to all voices. Themessage can be used in any inlet. The instance index specified byoverrides the current value of theattribute but leaves it unchanged after the message has been sent.

messages.name: threadcount
messages.digest: Set the number of threads used to divideinstances' audio processing
messages.description: The word, followed by a number, sets the number of threads used to divideinstances' audio processing. The default is the number of processor cores available in your computer. Typically, the number of threads should be set to the number of processor cores in your computer for best performance. This can also be accomplished by sending the message. If aobject has sixteen instances and the threadcount is 4, four of theinstances will process audio in each of four threads.

messages.name: up
messages.digest: Upsample the audio on the currently loaded patcher
messages.description: Use themessage followed by a number which is a power of two to upsample local DSP processing on the currently loaded patcher (e.g.,specifies 88200 Hz at a sampling rate of 44100 Hz). Upsampling is not dynamic. DSP must be restarted before the change can take effect. Although bothandare permissible messages to theobject, themessage takes precedence over.

messages.name: wclose
messages.digest: Close a numbered patcher instance's window
messages.description: Closes the window for the numbered instance specified by the argument. If no number argument is used,will close the patcher window with the highest numbered index.
